reasons: internal/execution/provenance.go:59-60 The scan now covers Agent, but the audit entry written on the very same call still carries the raw, unscrubbed name: SendDecision takes the record by value, so exportDecision's `record.Agent` is the pre-scrub string and it is passed as details["agent"] to recordContentScan. With the PR's own example (an agent named "민원 900101-1234568 담당", rrn=block) the RRN is refused at the HTTP boundary and then persisted verbatim in audit_events.details — and audit details are read back and shipped out again by store.AuditTrailEach (internal/store/audit.go:114). Before this change that path could not fire for an agent-name value (no findings -> recordContentScan returns early, as its own comment says), so the PR converts an external leak into a stored one. It contradicts recordContentScan's doc at internal/execution/contentscan.go:119-121 ("never the value itself") and dlp.Scan's at internal/dlp/dlp.go:~268 ("never logged and never stored"). Passing record.AgentID (already the audit subject) instead would keep the entry useful without storing the value.

internal/execution/provenance.go:233-236 Agent and Category are the same string by construction — internal/store/provenance.go:122 does `record.Category = record.Agent` — so scanning both reports every agent-name finding twice. Verified by calling scrubDecision directly with Agent=Category="민원 900101-1234568 담당": findings=2, Labels()=[주민등록번호 주민등록번호], Summary()="주민등록번호 1건, 주민등록번호 1건", and the operator-facing sentence becomes "결정 기록에 주민등록번호, 주민등록번호가 포함되어 보내지 않았습니다". That is the double-reporting scrubDecision's own comment (provenance.go:262-264, "an entry per field would tell the operator the same record left three times") and dlp's claim() mechanism (internal/dlp/dlp.go:~415, "so one value is reported once") both exist to prevent. The new test bakes it in rather than catching it: provenance_test.go:337 asserts exactly 3 findings for a single RRN that appears in two mirrored fields plus Model. Findings should be merged per class before they reach WithheldError/Summary, or Category should be scanned as the copy it is.
notes: The new tests do exercise the change: reverting decisionWords to the original three fields (Scenario/Reasoning/SourceURL) makes TestEveryWordInARecordIsScannedOnItsWayOut and TestEveryFieldOfARecordIsEitherScannedOrAnIdentifier fail with the expected messages. Working tree was restored afterwards.
go build ./..., go vet ./internal/... and go test ./internal/... all pass on HEAD.

The identifier exemption is sound and is defended by a real assertion (TestTheIdentifiersInARecordAreNotScanned first proves the account detector actually claims an all-digit uuid, then proves the ids are untouched). The reflection sweep covers all 15 string fields of DecisionRecord; OccurredAt/AgentVersion are correctly skipped as non-strings.
No scope creep: two files, both on the reported defect. Nothing irreversible — no migration, no external state; a plain revert restores prior behaviour.

Minor: the reflection test greps provenance.go for the literal loop line `for _, field := range decisionWords {`, so any reformatting of that line fails the test for a non-reason. Style only, not a merge blocker.

Redacting Model/RuntimeImage/Outcome/Source rewrites values a receiving system may key on. I checked the plausible false positive (a date-suffixed model name like gpt-4o-2024-05-13): the account detector's notPhone validator requires >=9 digits, so it does not fire. No concrete false positive found.
